notes: A: hostile Origin; B: no ns, Host other-ns.example.com; C: ns=other-ns, Host demo-test.example.com; D: no ns, Host other-ns.example.com:<port>; E: ns=demo-test, Host localhost:1234 (to see whether hello h follows Host).
requests holds the exact HTTP upgrade request text sent per connection (fixed Sec-WebSocket-Key).
rest holds REST GETs of /golden/origin on ns=demo-test, ns=other-ns and with no ns (Host 127.0.0.1) after all markers were written.

Observed with firebase-database-emulator-v4.11.2: Origin is not checked (101 for https://evil.example). Without ?ns the namespace is the first label of the Host header (other-ns.example.com -> other-ns, with or without port); when ?ns is present it wins over Host. The hello h field stays the emulator host:port whatever the Host header says. X-Firebase-Project-Id names the chosen namespace.
close initiated by the client (close frame with code 1000) on: A, B, C, D, E; the code recorded is what the client saw in the emulator's closing reply (1005 = the reply carried no status code).
